T0607.title: VLA Model
T0607.definition: An end-to-end model fusing visual perception, language understanding, and action output; the core decision-making brain of embodied-intelligence robots, mapping visual observations and language instructions to physical action sequences.
T0607.description: The VLA model is the key technology distinguishing embodied intelligence from traditional robots, with representatives like OpenVLA, RT-2, and Octo. It combines the perception-understanding capability of Vision-Language Models (VLM) with action generation, enabling robots to perform complex manipulation from natural-language instructions and visual observations. But VLA models inherit and amplify LLM/VLM vulnerabilities: adversarial examples, adversarial patches, jailbreaks, backdoors, and cross-modal injection attacks can translate directly into physical-action errors. Research like RoboPAIR jailbreak, UPA-RFAS adversarial patch, and DropVLA backdoor shows VLA models' physical-world attack surface far exceeds pure software models.
T0607.usageExample: A service robot driven by a VLA model, when receiving a grasp-cup instruction, may mis-grab a nearby thermos if attacked by an adversarial patch, causing scalding.
